resolved.title: property 装饰器
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Properties[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

[b]Properties [/b]provide a way of customizing access to instance attributes. 
They are created by putting the [b]property[/b] decorator above a method, which means when the instance attribute with the same name as the method is accessed, the method will be called instead. 
One common use of a property is to make an attribute [b]read-only[/b].

[s0l0!-header][b]Example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="420"]class Pizza:
  def __init__(self, toppings):
    self.toppings = toppings
    
  [b]@property[/b]
  def pineapple_allowed(self):
    return False

pizza = Pizza(["cheese", "tomato"])
print(pizza.pineapple_allowed)
pizza.pineapple_allowed = True[/code]
[note][b]Run the code[/b] and see how it works![/note]

resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Properties[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

Properties can also be set by defining [b]setter/getter[/b] functions.
The [b]setter [/b]function sets the corresponding property's value.
The [b]getter [/b]gets the value.
To define a [b]setter[/b], you need to use a decorator of the same name as the property, followed by a dot and the [b]setter[/b] keyword.
The same applies to defining [b]getter [/b]functions.

[s0l0!-header][b]Example:[/b][/s0l0!-header][code format="py" codeId="950"]class Pizza:
  def __init__(self, toppings):
    self.toppings = toppings
    self._pineapple_allowed = False

  @property
  def pineapple_allowed(self):
    return self._pineapple_allowed

  [b]@pineapple_allowed.setter[/b]
  def pineapple_allowed(self, value):
    if value:
      password = input("Enter the password: ")
      if password == "Sw0rdf1sh!":
        self._pineapple_allowed = value
      else:
        raise ValueError("Alert! Intruder!")

pizza = Pizza(["cheese", "tomato"])
print(pizza.pineapple_allowed)
pizza.pineapple_allowed = True
print(pizza.pineapple_allowed)[/code]

content.title: 类属性 - 是否存活

resolved.title: 角色生存状态检测
resolved.problem_statement_md:
我们正在改进之前编写的游戏，现在需要添一个**isAlive**属性，如果生命值大于0，则返回**True**。

通过添加**isAlive**属性完成代码。
resolved.problem_statement_en_md:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Properties[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

We are improving our game and need to add an [b]isAlive[/b] property, which returns [b]True[/b] if the lives count is greater than 0.
Complete the code by adding the [b]isAlive[/b] property.
[note]The code uses a while loop to hit the [b]Player[/b], until its lives count becomes 0, using the [b]isAlive[/b] property to make the condition.[/note]
resolved.hint_md: 该代码使用`while`循环来打击`hit`玩家，直到它的生命值变成`0`，并使用**isAlive**属性来做条件。

code_templates.template:
class Player:
    def __init__(self, name, lives):
        self.name = name
        self._lives = lives

    def hit(self):
        self._lives -= 1
    
    #请完善代码
    

# 以下代码勿改
p = Player("pythontip", int(input()))
i = 1
while True:
    p.hit()
    print("Hit # " + str(i))
    i += 1
    if not p.isAlive:
        print("Game Over")
        break
